entries.boundary: Search close attempt after public query
entries.reason: Preserve an established sanitized query failure or cancellation. Diagnose secondary cleanup failure by class only; with no primary, propagate cleanup failure. Cleanup is attempted, not guaranteed.
entries.diagnostic_path: Class-only cleanup warning and established primary propagation

entries.boundary: Terminal Blob summary attempt during primary failure or cancellation
entries.reason: A secondary terminal summary failure must not replace established run failure or cancellation. Without a primary it propagates. Summary persistence and client cleanup are attempted, not guaranteed.
entries.diagnostic_path: Class-only terminal-summary warning, original primary propagation and outer resource cleanup attempt

entries.boundary: Delegated-user retrieval query to the existing HTTP 502 envelope
entries.reason: The public retrieval contract hides downstream query payloads and returns 502 on query failure, including unexpected adapter failures. Feature gating and delegated-user validation run before this boundary, and this record does not exempt authentication or authorize an elevated read.
entries.diagnostic_path: Exception-class-only query diagnostic and HTTP 502 preserved across attempted Search cleanup

entries.boundary: SharePoint purge Search-client close
entries.reason: Preserve the primary purge exception while still attempting Blob, Key Vault and credential closure if Search close fails. Only resource disposal is covered; search scans and delete confirmation propagate independently.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe Search cleanup warning and subsequent resource close attempts

entries.boundary: SharePoint purge log-storage client close
entries.reason: The inherited independent Blob cleanup must not replace a scan/delete failure or skip Key Vault and credential disposal. This proposal cannot suppress storage construction, probing or primary document operations.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe Blob cleanup warning followed by Key Vault and credential close

entries.boundary: SharePoint purge Key Vault client close
entries.reason: Preserve the original primary exception and continue credential cleanup if the Key Vault client cannot close. Secret retrieval, configuration and Graph authorization are outside this disposal-only boundary.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe Key Vault cleanup warning and independent credential closure

entries.boundary: SharePoint purge credential close after client disposal
entries.reason: Closing an already used credential must not replace the original purge exception or relabel confirmed primary results. Token acquisition and identity selection are not recoverable under this proposal.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe credential cleanup warning with original purge failure preserved

entries.boundary: Existing time-bounded optional SharePoint purge summary wrapper
entries.reason: A secondary dashboard-summary failure must not override the actual purge failure. Inner serialization and storage operations now propagate defects to this one bounded wrapper instead of independently swallowing them; scans and deletion are outside the wrapper.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe summary-write failure warning; original primary exception remains observable

entries.boundary: Failed purge summary observation followed by original exception propagation
entries.reason: The worker must record failed terminal status for count, late-page and unconfirmed-delete failures while re-raising to its scheduler/audit caller. This observation does not allow a finished summary after any failed deletion.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe RUN-ERROR, failed summary, original exception and outer resource cleanup

entries.boundary: Delete request/result projection to explicit per-batch failed counts
entries.reason: Preserve the established deleted/failed return contract while refusing missing, duplicate, malformed or unconfirmed SDK results. An unexpected adapter/result defect marks the entire affected batch failed, never successful; the run then propagates a failed purge. Logging is outside the protected success-count projection.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe batch error, per-item delete-failed events and positive docsFailedDelete

entries.boundary: Optional audit environment label after authoritative governance validation
entries.reason: Preserve the existing unknown audit-context label when this diagnostic-only lookup fails. GovernanceSettings.from_config executes outside this catch, so primary provider errors and contradictory governance settings still fail startup.
entries.diagnostic_path: Audit warning with exception class, unknown context label and unchanged resolved governance

entries.boundary: Constructing an iterator over an untrusted audit Mapping protocol
entries.reason: Arbitrary Mapping implementations can raise exceptions unrelated to built-in dict errors. The unchanged sanitizer must omit this optional value and record its path, not allow hostile protocol behavior to change primary ingestion or export unsanitized data.
entries.diagnostic_path: Bounded omitted_fields path in the sanitized event; no hostile value or error text exported

entries.boundary: Constructing an iterator over an untrusted audit Sequence protocol
entries.reason: Sequence.__iter__ is arbitrary caller code. Preserve bounded omission of a sequence whose iterator cannot be constructed, with required event identifiers intact; this is an audit-only sanitization boundary, not a source-document fallback.
entries.diagnostic_path: Optional value absent and its bounded path present in omitted_fields

entries.boundary: Late Mapping/Sequence protocol failure during bounded audit traversal
entries.reason: An iterator may be constructed successfully and then raise while obtaining a nested key/value. Preserve fail-closed omission of the entire affected optional value and cycle-state cleanup instead of leaking partial unsanitized data or affecting primary work.
entries.diagnostic_path: Bounded omitted_fields path and required event identifiers preserved

entries.boundary: Untrusted omitted/truncated path sequences supplied to audit sanitization
entries.reason: Even caller-provided diagnostic sequences can implement hostile iteration. Preserve the existing bounded omission marker rather than exporting their payloads or letting optional audit diagnostics affect ingestion.
entries.diagnostic_path: The failed diagnostic field is itself recorded in omitted_fields

entries.boundary: Existing Search query adapter explicit error envelope
entries.reason: Keep the published documents/count/error result shape for unexpected query failures, now without downstream payload text. Retrieval translates error to HTTP 502. Destructive image maintenance uses a separate complete streaming path that propagates failures and cannot interpret this envelope as an empty successful index.
entries.diagnostic_path: Exception-class-only diagnostic and nonempty error field with no returned documents

entries.boundary: Existing endpoint constructor fallback to configured connection string or environment adapter
entries.reason: H1 implementation chooses only existing configured sources: endpoint, then configured connection string, otherwise the existing environment adapter only with allow_environment_variables opt-in. Credential chain, Key Vault credentials, selector order and existing nonempty-string opt-in parsing are unchanged. Exhausted remote sources propagate; unavailable environment keys retain required-key failure semantics. Successful fallback has an explicit safe diagnostic. SDK merge evidence uses declared provider 2.5.0. This exact broad-handler proposal is not active approval.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe endpoint-fallback diagnostic, identical configured selectors and Key Vault credential on fallback, actual selected fallback values or propagated connection-string error; no new source or permission

entries.boundary: SharePoint indexer Search close after every run or partial initialization
entries.reason: Search cleanup must not override the original run/configuration failure or skip storage, Key Vault and credential closure. The public run now guarantees this cleanup even when datasource configuration fails before work begins. Search operations and confirmation are not covered.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe Search cleanup warning, original primary exception and remaining close attempts

entries.boundary: SharePoint indexer optional log-storage client close
entries.reason: The existing independent storage cleanup must not mask a primary failure or prevent Key Vault and credential closure. Storage initialization/probing/writes are separately narrowed to declared SDK errors; this record covers close only.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe Blob cleanup warning and independent subsequent resource closures

entries.boundary: SharePoint indexer Key Vault adapter close
entries.reason: A Key Vault close failure must leave the primary run exception intact and still attempt credential closure. Secret retrieval and Graph token acquisition are not optional under this record and remain outside the cleanup boundary.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe Key Vault cleanup warning without secret or dependency payload

entries.boundary: SharePoint indexer final chained-credential close
entries.reason: Retain independent closure after the Search, Blob and Key Vault attempts; arbitrary credential close failures warn without replacing the primary exception. This does not excuse authentication or identity configuration failures.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe credential cleanup warning and original primary exception identity

entries.boundary: SharePoint run failed-summary observation followed by exception propagation
entries.reason: A failed collection must mark the run failed and propagate to the scheduler/audit wrapper, not become a finished run with zero failed items. The handler preserves the existing summary schema with safe error text, then re-raises. Its outer resource guard closes clients on configuration, collection and cancellation paths.
entries.diagnostic_path: Failed terminal summary, safe run error and original exception propagation

entries.boundary: Existing bounded optional run-summary persistence wrapper
entries.reason: Run-summary persistence is a secondary diagnostic side effect and must not replace a primary run result when storage, serialization or its adapter fails. Inner retries now handle only SDK/timeouts and parser errors; this single outer wrapper contains unexpected diagnostic failures with a safe warning and the existing total timeout.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe summary failure/timeout warning; primary exception remains authoritative

entries.boundary: SharePoint per-item processing failure, retry/block state and failed-count translation
entries.reason: The existing per-item boundary must record explicit failed items while siblings proceed. Permission acquisition now occurs within this bounded operation, so its failure records an error and cannot create empty ACLs or unobserved task exceptions. Failures before this boundary propagate through observed collection tasks; cancellation is not converted into a file success.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe per-file error, failed item counter and no Search operation after ACL failure

entries.boundary: Blob run summary failure observation followed by original exception propagation
entries.reason: The worker attempts to persist failed terminal state while propagating the original index-scan/source failure to the scheduler and audit wrapper. Arbitrary failures are observed, not converted to successful completion. Terminal summary and resource cleanup are attempted, not guaranteed; secondary summary errors cannot replace the primary.
entries.diagnostic_path: Failed summary attempt and safe error class followed by re-raising the original exception

entries.boundary: Existing per-Blob failed-document result and retry/block tracking
entries.reason: A failed metadata/read/chunk/index operation must become an explicit error record consumed by run aggregation, preserving retry/block history and allowing independent files to proceed. ACL acquisition errors now reach this boundary instead of becoming empty security fields. No failed file is counted as indexed; temporary-file cleanup no longer replaces early metadata failures.
entries.diagnostic_path: status=error, safe error class, failed per-file history and no download after ACL acquisition failure

entries.boundary: Blob indexer Search client close
entries.reason: An arbitrary Search close failure must not mask the primary document/run failure or prevent Blob and credential closure. This preserves independent resource cleanup with a safe warning; Search reads, writes and confirmation are outside the handler.
entries.diagnostic_path: Search cleanup warning, original primary exception and subsequent close attempts

entries.boundary: Blob indexer storage client close
entries.reason: Storage client close is independent cleanup after primary processing. Failure must not replace the original exception or skip credential closure; it is not a waiver for source metadata/download or staging operations.
entries.diagnostic_path: Blob cleanup warning and continued credential close without changing the primary outcome

entries.boundary: Blob indexer chained credential close
entries.reason: The final credential close may fail independently of primary work; retain the original exception and report safe cleanup diagnostics. Credential construction, token acquisition and authorization are never covered by this record.
entries.diagnostic_path: Credential cleanup warning while the original primary exception propagates

entries.boundary: Blob purger Search client close
entries.reason: A Search close failure cannot replace the purge failure or prevent the remaining resource closures. This is a separate exact site from indexer cleanup; confirmed deletion and exhausted Search retries remain authoritative and are not waived.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe Search cleanup warning followed by Blob and credential closure

entries.boundary: Blob purger storage client close
entries.reason: Retain the pre-existing independent cleanup contract: a failed storage close warns safely but cannot mask the original purge error or skip credential close. Source enumeration and log writes are outside this exact boundary.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe Blob cleanup warning and unchanged primary exception

entries.boundary: Blob purger chained credential close
entries.reason: Credential cleanup runs after independent Search and Blob close attempts and must not override the primary purge outcome. This proposal concerns closure only, not any credential/authentication operation needed to perform a purge.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe credential cleanup warning; primary exception identity is retained

entries.boundary: Existing background startup log-retention task
entries.reason: Log retention has always been isolated from service startup and independently scheduled ingestion. One shared boundary replaces the duplicated startup/cleanup-only handlers. Arbitrary cleanup defects are reported without exposing payloads; they do not prevent other startup jobs or scheduler shutdown. Actual deletion totals are confirmed separately, and cancellation is not caught.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe log-cleanup error class, independent workers and normal scheduler shutdown

entries.boundary: Established ordered startup worker isolation after each authoritative worker outcome
entries.reason: Startup continues independent sources after a failed worker, unlike cron/manual execution which must propagate its failure. Each worker still emits a failed audit outcome and releases its running slot before this outer isolation boundary reports the error. No failed indexing result is converted to success, and cancellation explicitly propagates.
entries.diagnostic_path: Failed worker audit event and safe startup job/error-class diagnostic

entries.boundary: API-key text-embedding skill per-record error envelope
entries.reason: The existing skill reports a failed record with empty data and nonempty errors while continuing independent records. Arbitrary embedding adapter defects must retain that explicit failure shape rather than abort the entire skill request or fabricate a vector. Only safe diagnostics are returned; authorization remains outside the boundary.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe embedding error in the existing 200 per-record envelope and error-class log

entries.boundary: Pre-existing optional original-file Blob persistence before direct indexing
entries.reason: Original-file persistence is explicitly best-effort in this endpoint. Its adapter/configuration failure adds a warning and retains the established fallback path; it cannot prevent chunking or reverse a separately confirmed Search upload. This is not a source download, indexing or authorization exemption.
entries.diagnostic_path: Original file not persisted warning and safe error-class log; Search independently confirms indexedChunks

entries.boundary: Direct-upload per-record document chunker invocation
entries.reason: The established outer record boundary handles constructor/metadata/orchestration failures outside the chunker's own errors-list translation. It must return that record's explicit chunking error, skip its upload and retain the batch envelope. It never substitutes chunks for a failed chunker or changes the API-key gate.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe chunking error, unchanged recordId, no Search upload for the failed record

entries.boundary: Existing per-chunk embedding and explicit Search document construction
entries.reason: Malformed chunk fields or embedding adapter failures remain explicit record errors while successfully prepared sibling chunks can be uploaded. A failed chunk is not appended to the batch; no placeholder vector or indexed count is invented. Arbitrary adapter failures require the existing translation boundary, not a giant SDK exception tuple.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe embedding/preparation errors and no upload/count for failed chunks

entries.boundary: Existing always-200 read-only identity state probe
entries.reason: The source explicitly distinguishes this state probe from an access check: invalid tokens or validator failures yield isAdmin=false without raising or token logging. Preserve that public response even for unexpected validator failures. This does not guard mutations; require_admin independently verifies the bearer and propagates failures.
entries.diagnostic_path: authEnabled=true and isAdmin=false, with no token/error payload

entries.boundary: Read-only configuration listing optional canEdit state probe
entries.reason: The existing configuration view remains readable without a valid token; arbitrary validator failures must not grant edit access or change this read response to an error. Only the display hint falls back to false. PUT authorization and actual configuration reads/writes remain outside this handler and must fail visibly.
entries.diagnostic_path: canEdit=false without logging credentials; independent Admin mutation gate

entries.boundary: Manual enqueue failure with matching reservation rollback
entries.reason: Any APScheduler/plugin failure after reserving the shared running slot must release only this trigger's reservation and return the established safe HTTP 500, never queued/202. Keeping this exact translation is necessary for run-now retryability and singleton/lock semantics, including unexpected scheduler defects.
entries.diagnostic_path: Failed to schedule job HTTP 500 and safe job/error-class log

entries.boundary: Unblock log download/read failure translation before any mutation
entries.reason: Stage 2 P2: only ResourceNotFoundError maps to 404. Other download/read failures become a generic 500; invalid JSON or a non-object log has a separate sanitized integrity error. Failed reads/parsing cannot upload or invalidate cache. Actual unblock writes are outside this proposal.
entries.diagnostic_path: Static error diagnostic without exception payload; sanitized read/integrity 500 or confirmed-missing 404; no unblock write attempted

entries.boundary: Per-key schedule application after a confirmed durable configuration write
entries.reason: Scheduler failures do not undo durable AppConfig writes. The established partial-application response must retain applied and report reschedule failed with 207 while allowing other keys to be attempted. This is distinct from optional cache refresh, which retains 200/applied, and from actual write confirmation.
entries.diagnostic_path: 207 applied/failed/rescheduled payload and safe key/error-class diagnostic

entries.boundary: Explicit apply operation's independent per-schedule error aggregation
entries.reason: An arbitrary scheduler failure must be included in the explicit HTTP 500 failed-key result while remaining schedules can still be applied. The handler never returns status=ok when any application failed. Cache refresh/configuration reads are outside the boundary and propagate; this is not optional refresh recovery.
entries.diagnostic_path: HTTP 500 with failed and rescheduled keys, safe scheduler error class

entries.boundary: Documented panel feedback Cosmos read-to-502 translation
entries.reason: The shipped endpoint and existing RuntimeError regression require a sanitized 502 for a failed adapter read, not a silently filtered list or unhandled 500. Authentication and stored-document schema validation remain outside this specific handler. Preserve the established public failure mapping for arbitrary adapter failures.
entries.diagnostic_path: Failed to read feedback from Cosmos DB HTTP 502, payload-free error log

entries.boundary: Documented panel feedback Cosmos write-to-502 translation
entries.reason: The explicit existing write contract maps raised adapter failures to sanitized 502 and must never return created/201 after an unconfirmed write. Both unexpected exceptions and None-result controls are covered by maintained tests. Request validation and Admin authorization are outside this boundary.
entries.diagnostic_path: Failed to write feedback to Cosmos DB HTTP 502 without comment/tag/error payload

entries.boundary: Existing optional feedback enrichment of the jobs/files overview
entries.reason: H2 implementation adds feedback.available to the legacy overview typed response while retaining integer count fields and jobs/files availability. Complete reads, including genuine empty feedback, are available=true. Constructor, read, pagination or aggregation failures yield available=false and zero placeholders, never partial observations. The local frontend uses the separate /panel/overview/metrics schema; its privacy-suppressed null semantics, shared schema bytes, authorization and writes are unchanged. External legacy consumers must honor availability; published-doc coordination remains required. This exact broad-handler proposal remains inactive.
entries.diagnostic_path: Sanitized server warning and feedback.available=false; jobs/files survive and incomplete counts are discarded

entries.boundary: Strict delegated operator metrics metadata-store query
entries.reason: Unlike optional legacy overview enrichment, the versioned operator metrics endpoint explicitly requires a sanitized 502 when metadata counts cannot be obtained. Arbitrary constructor/query failures cannot produce zero counts or a success response. Gate and delegated authorization execute before this boundary.
entries.diagnostic_path: Panel metadata store query failed HTTP 502 with correlation-id diagnostic

entries.boundary: Strict delegated operator metrics corpus-control count query
entries.reason: A failed corpus-control query must invalidate the metrics response even when metadata counts succeeded. This separate exact boundary preserves the documented 502 and prevents partial counts from appearing authoritative. Failure evidence reaches this second query independently of the first store.
entries.diagnostic_path: Corpus control store query failed HTTP 502 with safe correlation-id log

entries.boundary: Delegated corpus-curation queue store query-to-502 translation
entries.reason: The existing public queue contract requires an explicit 502 rather than an empty queue or new cursor on adapter failure. Constructor and query defects are covered; cursor validation and principal binding execute before this boundary and are not relaxed.
entries.diagnostic_path: Corpus control store query failed HTTP 502 and correlation-id diagnostic

entries.boundary: Final curation decision write-to-502 translation after exact domain errors
entries.reason: Unexpected write failures must preserve the documented safe 502 instead of returning an unconfirmed decision. Item-not-found, conflict and exhausted concurrency retain their earlier specific handlers. This final boundary does not authorize callers, retry writes, infer success or change idempotency.
entries.diagnostic_path: Corpus control store write failed HTTP 502 with safe correlation-id log

entries.boundary: Existing format-chunker orchestration boundary returning terminal document errors
entries.reason: A format-specific chunker failure must become an explicit failed-document errors list consumed by ingestion, not successful chunks or a suppressed cancellation. The established result shape is retained with a safe message. Arbitrary format implementation exceptions require this one translation boundary; lower SDK/parser retries and optional image handling are narrowed separately. BaseException and metadata failures outside this boundary propagate.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe document processing error and nonempty terminal errors list; no dependency payload

entries.boundary: Existing per-document NL2SQL processing failure result consumed by run aggregation
entries.reason: The established boundary converts a failed properties/read/embedding/upload operation to an explicit error record and failed per-kind count so other documents can proceed. Arbitrary adapter implementation failures must never be retried as missing documents or counted as indexed. This proposal covers only this explicit failed-result translation; expected optional-log operations are separately narrowed and cancellation is not caught.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe error-class message, per-file status=error and run itemsFailed; no raw dependency payload

entries.boundary: Search client close in NL2SQL indexing run finally block
entries.reason: A Search cleanup failure must not replace the original listing/indexing outcome or skip subsequent Blob and credential cleanup. This preserves the pre-existing lifecycle contract while making cleanup failure visible. It covers close only, not search, upload or result aggregation.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe Search cleanup warning; primary exception or confirmed summary remains authoritative

entries.boundary: BlobServiceClient close after NL2SQL indexing
entries.reason: A Blob close failure must not replace a primary run failure, reverse a confirmed document result, or prevent the chained credential from closing. The existing independent cleanup sequencing is preserved with an explicit warning; no source download/listing or durable write is exempted.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe Blob cleanup warning, followed by credential close

entries.boundary: Chained credential close after NL2SQL indexing
entries.reason: The last resource-close operation must not mask the primary run failure or convert confirmed document totals into an indexing failure. Both successful and failed runs inject a non-SDK close failure and prove that all owned cleanup calls are attempted. Credential creation/token acquisition and authorization are outside this proposal.
entries.diagnostic_path: Safe credential cleanup warning without changing the primary result

entries.boundary: Optional token-integrity debug diagnostics before independent JWT verification
entries.reason: This pre-existing debug-only boundary must not change authorization when a configured logging handler or token-length diagnostic fails. It neither returns claims nor skips the subsequent signature, issuer, audience and expiry checks. A real signed-token test injects a failing diagnostic sink and still executes full verification.
entries.diagnostic_path: Optional sink may be unavailable; primary JWT verification and its explicit HTTP failure remain authoritative

entries.boundary: Optional Microsoft Graph audience warning, not the audience validation operation
entries.reason: The established warning is diagnostic only. Logging sink failures must not replace the actual audience rejection or bypass verification. The failure test uses a real signed Graph-audience token and a failing warning sink; JWT verification still returns the established 403 Invalid token audience outcome. No decoder, key acquisition, signature or authorization operation is inside this proposal.
entries.diagnostic_path: The authoritative JWT validation returns an explicit 403 audience failure even if the optional warning cannot be emitted

entries.boundary: Per-record direct Search batch upload in the API-key ingestion endpoint
entries.reason: The established endpoint returns a 200 envelope with explicit per-record errors instead of aborting all submitted records. SDK transport and malformed-response failures must remain failed records, never inferred uploads. Confirmation is computed from matching requested keys before indexedChunks is assigned; this proposal does not cover chunking, embedding, optional Blob persistence or authorization.
entries.diagnostic_path: Per-record Batch indexing error plus stage/exception-class log without downstream payload

entries.boundary: Optional audit sanitization before export
entries.reason: A sanitizer defect must drop an unsafe audit event, not fail an already-running ingestion operation. This record covers only the unexpected sanitizer catch, not source/configuration failures.
entries.diagnostic_path: gptrag.audit_warning: dropped event type and exception class, without exception payload

entries.boundary: Optional audit logger/exporter invocation
entries.reason: A failed logger/exporter must not reverse a confirmed Search outcome or turn a successful worker into a failure. Only the audit side effect is dropped; the primary result is unchanged.
entries.diagnostic_path: gptrag.audit_warning: failed export stage, event type and exception class only

entries.boundary: Run context manager observing the primary worker failure
entries.reason: Record exactly one failed terminal event and re-raise the same primary exception. The context-variable cleanup must still run; this catch never converts an indexing/purge failure to success.
entries.diagnostic_path: Correlated ingestion.run.failed event; original exception propagates to the worker caller

entries.boundary: Optional document audit projection of an existing Search response
entries.reason: Malformed audit projection must not alter the caller's primary SDK result. The write adapter separately validates confirmation; this catch does not approve or synthesize a successful upload/delete.
entries.diagnostic_path: gptrag.audit_warning: document emission failed, with exception class but no source or exception payload

entries.boundary: Local cache refresh after confirmed durable App Configuration writes
entries.reason: The established PUT contract treats only this post-write refresh as best-effort. A refresh failure must not relabel an already applied durable write as failed. Explicit reload/apply operations, remote writes and primary provider reads retain their independent failure contracts.
entries.diagnostic_path: Warning naming the post-write cache-refresh stage and exception class, without downstream payload

entries.boundary: Closing the purger-owned Search adapter in run finalization
entries.reason: Search transport cleanup must be attempted but cannot replace the original purge failure or reverse an already confirmed Search outcome. A failed close must still allow Blob and credential cleanup.
entries.diagnostic_path: NL2SQL Search-client cleanup warning with exception class only

entries.boundary: Closing the purger-owned Blob client in run finalization
entries.reason: Preserve the existing non-masking cleanup boundary while making its failure visible. A Blob close failure must not skip credential cleanup, manufacture a finished summary after a failed purge, or invalidate confirmed primary work.
entries.diagnostic_path: NL2SQL Blob-client cleanup warning with exception class only

entries.boundary: Closing the purger-owned credential after its clients
entries.reason: Credential finalization is not a new indexing/deletion operation. Preserve the original primary exception or confirmed result if credential cleanup fails, but emit a safe warning rather than silently passing.
entries.diagnostic_path: NL2SQL credential-cleanup warning with exception class only

review.rationale: Explicit administrative initial-adoption approval by Paulo (@placerda) activates exactly the 67 individually justified existing records at 0ae3759356935830c532ce3f2c48d3753b01da73. This is not independent GitHub review or a green bootstrap claim. Same-run failure evidence remains mandatory; no record exempts unconfirmed indexing, deletion or authorization.
